plan: Key changes: (1) a Vite build of React and TypeScript sources, where before nothing could be built and after npm run build writes dist and the app page shows the Ada trial heading drawn by React; (2) a Vitest harness, where before there were no unit tests and after npm test runs them with coverage; (3) a Playwright harness, where before there were no browser tests and after npm run test:e2e builds, serves and tests the app in Chromium; (4) a CI workflow and patch coverage script. Run the existing e2e and unit tests, implement TC-1 to TC-5 from the design, add checks TC-6 to TC-12 for the Code review findings, the dev server, the coverage file and the harnesses' failure paths, then play the walkthrough.

Installed packages from the lockfile and Chromium

remaining: The QA person reviews the run at the Test run gate
decisions: F1 low, confirmed, high confidence: the main entry unit test leaves its React root mounted and the unit run prints an act warning (TC-6). Developers running verbose unit tests notice; not a user path.
F2 low, confirmed, high confidence: npm run test:e2e builds the app again after CI has built it, so CI builds twice (TC-7). CI time only.

F3 low, confirmed, high confidence: package.json does not list @testing-library/dom; installed without peer dependencies the unit tests cannot load (TC-8). Developers with legacy peer settings notice.

F4 medium, unconfirmed, read in code: the CI coverage step runs the pull request's own script with a token that can write commit statuses, so a person with push access could post any status. Cannot be run in the QA environment.
F5 low, unconfirmed, read in code: on a fork pull request the coverage status job fails because its token is read-only.
F6 low, unconfirmed, read in code: the coverage/patch status is computed from coverage the pull request itself produced, so it is advice, not a control.
F7 low, unconfirmed, read in code: the GitHub actions are pinned to the movable v4 tag.
F8 low, confirmed by reading .gitignore: the pattern coverage/ has no leading slash, so it also matches test/coverage/ and plain git add skips the kept coverage tests.
F9 low, design gap: the project's browser tests run in one Desktop Chrome project and the app has no themes, so the browser coverage tests run at one width and one theme only.

TC-4 failed twice on its first run because my own pattern expected app.spec.ts without its e2e folder; the project's run itself passed. Explained away as a test fault, fixed, and the whole file ran again and passed.
uncertain: F4: whether the CI coverage step should run the script from the base branch instead of the pull request; a security decision for the QA person
F8: whether Ada commits test/coverage despite the coverage/ ignore pattern; if not, the kept coverage tests are lost
run_id is set to the brief id, as the run id was not given

suggested_follow_ups: Run scripts/patch-coverage.mjs from the base branch checkout in the coverage-status job, or drop statuses write from the step that runs pull request code
Change the .gitignore pattern coverage/ to /coverage/ so test/coverage is kept
Unmount the React root in the main entry test's cleanup
Let CI skip the second build, for example reuse the dist that the Build step wrote
